user.title: Welcome to SunBridge
user.description:
SunBridge turns this Home Assistant into the server your Growatt datalogger (ShineLan-X or similar) uploads to, so your solar readings stay on your own network. No cloud account, no extra software.

The next screens ask for a port, show you exactly what to change on the datalogger's web page, then wait for the datalogger to connect and show you what it found.

**Simple** creates the core sensors with sensible defaults. **Advanced** adds more sensors, a datalogger allow-list and the upload interval.

data_description.mode: You can change this later from Configure.

port.title: Choose the Port
port.description:
The datalogger will connect to this Home Assistant at the address and port below. Home Assistant detected its own address on your network as **{address}**. Check it, and correct it if Home Assistant has more than one network connection.

**Before you go on:** SunBridge listens on this port on every network interface of this Home Assistant, and the datalogger's protocol has no password. Any device that can reach the port can connect and send readings. That is why SunBridge answers only the datalogger it finds during setup: its serial goes in the allow-list. Keep the port reachable from your own network only, never forward it from the internet.

data_description.port: The TCP port to listen on. 5279 is the port Growatt dataloggers use, so keep it unless something else needs it.
data_description.address: The IPv4 address the datalogger will send to, for example 192.0.2.10. It is only used for the instructions on the next screen.

point.title: Point Your Datalogger Here
point.description:
Do this in daylight: the datalogger is powered by the inverter, so it is off when there is no sun.

1. Find the datalogger's own IP address in your router's list of connected devices, and open that address in a browser.
2. Log in with the user name and password printed on the datalogger's label (often `admin` / `admin`).
3. Open **Network Setting** and note down the values there, so you can go back to Growatt's cloud later.
4. Set **ResolvDomain** to **OFF**, **Server IP** to `{address}` and **Server port** to `{port}`. Click **Save**.
5. Open **Datalogger Setting**. Set **Reboot** to **yes** and click **Save**.

The datalogger restarts and connects here within a few minutes. Press **Next** once you have saved, and SunBridge starts listening.

found.title: Datalogger Found
found.description:
Your datalogger connected and sent a record SunBridge could read.

Datalogger serial: **{datalogger}**
Inverter serial: **{inverter}**

SunBridge will answer only this datalogger. To accept a different one later, open **Configure** and choose **Advanced**.

Continue to finish. Live readings appear with the next upload (every five minutes by default).

not_found.title: No Datalogger Yet
not_found.description:
Nothing arrived on port {port} in {minutes} minutes.

Check that the datalogger's Server IP is `{address}`, its Server port is `{port}`, ResolvDomain is OFF, and that it was rebooted. At night the datalogger is off: that is normal, and it connects once the sun is up.

**Finish now** keeps SunBridge listening on port {port}, which Home Assistant has checked it can open. No datalogger has been seen yet, so the allow-list stays empty and SunBridge answers any datalogger that connects; **Settings → System → Repairs** says so. Once your datalogger has connected, SunBridge puts its serial in the allow-list the next time it starts (a restart or a reload), or you can add it yourself from **Configure** by choosing **Advanced**.

menu_options.finish: Finish now: the port is ready, no datalogger seen yet

advanced.title: Advanced Settings
advanced.description:
The datalogger found during setup is already in the allow-list, so SunBridge will answer only that datalogger. Leave the list empty to accept any datalogger, which anything on your network could then pretend to be.

The upload interval is set on the datalogger's own web page (its Data Transfer Interval). Enter the same value here. SunBridge does not change the datalogger: it uses this to decide when live readings are out of date.

data_description.allowed_serials: Accept only these dataloggers, by serial, separated by commas: up to 10, each 1 to 30 letters and digits. Leave empty to accept any datalogger.
data_description.upload_interval: Minutes between the datalogger's uploads, as set on its web page (default 5).

reconfigure.title: Change the Port
reconfigure.description:
SunBridge listens on port {port} now. Enter a new port and Home Assistant checks it can open it, then moves the listener there. If the move fails, SunBridge goes back to port {port}; if even that fails, this form says so and **Settings → System → Repairs** names the port to free.

Afterwards, set the same **Server port** on the datalogger's web page (**Network Setting**) and reboot it, or it keeps sending to the old port.

data_description.port: The TCP port to listen on. 5279 is the port Growatt dataloggers use.

error.port_unavailable: Something else is already listening on this port. Pick another one, and set the same port on the datalogger.
error.invalid_address: Enter an IPv4 address, such as 192.0.2.10.
error.invalid_serial: A serial may only contain the letters A to Z and the digits 0 to 9.
error.port_in_use_by_entry: Another SunBridge entry already listens on this port.
error.serial_too_long: A datalogger serial is at most 30 characters long.
error.duplicate_serial: The same serial is in the list twice.

abort.already_configured: SunBridge is already listening on port {port}. Two listeners cannot share a port: to change that entry, use Configure on it, or choose another port for a second datalogger.
abort.reconfigure_successful: SunBridge now listens on the new port. Set the same Server port on the datalogger if you have not already.
abort.port_rollback_failed: SunBridge could not move to the new port, and could not go back to port {port} either, so it is not listening now. Its settings are back on port {port}. Free that port (stop whatever else is using it), then reload SunBridge from its integration page. **Settings → System → Repairs** shows this until SunBridge listens again.

progress.wait_for_datalogger: Waiting for your datalogger on `{address}` port `{port}`. This page moves on by itself as soon as the datalogger sends its first record. It listens for up to {minutes} minutes; after a reboot the datalogger usually connects within two or three.

create_entry.default:
SunBridge is listening.

To count your solar production in the Energy dashboard, open **Settings → Dashboards → Energy**, choose **Add solar production** under **Solar panels**, and pick **Energy total** from the **Solar Inverter** device. SunBridge does not change your Energy settings itself.

init.title: SunBridge Settings
init.description: Saving reloads the listener: open connections are closed and the datalogger reconnects. To change the port, use **Reconfigure** instead.

data_description.mode: Simple creates the core sensors. Advanced adds the extra sensors, and lets you edit the allow-list and the upload interval.

advanced.title: Advanced Settings
advanced.description: The upload interval is set on the datalogger's own web page (its Data Transfer Interval). Enter the same value here. SunBridge does not change the datalogger: it uses this to decide when live readings are out of date.

data_description.allowed_serials: Accept only these dataloggers, by serial, separated by commas: up to 10, each 1 to 30 letters and digits. Leave empty to accept any datalogger.
data_description.upload_interval: Minutes between the datalogger's uploads, as set on its web page (default 5).

error.serial_too_long: A datalogger serial is at most 30 characters long.
error.duplicate_serial: The same serial is in the list twice.

allow_list_empty.title: {title} answers any datalogger
allow_list_empty.description:
SunBridge on port {port} has an empty allow-list and has not seen a datalogger yet, so it answers any datalogger that connects. Anything on your network could pretend to be one.

Once your datalogger has connected, SunBridge puts its serial in the allow-list the next time it starts (a restart or a reload of the integration), and this message goes away. To set it now, open **Configure** on the SunBridge entry, choose **Advanced**, and enter the datalogger's serial (it is on the datalogger's label and on its device page).

allow_list_ambiguous.title: {title} answers any datalogger
allow_list_ambiguous.description:
SunBridge on port {port} has an empty allow-list, so it answers any datalogger that connects. It knows {count} dataloggers, so it cannot tell which one is yours and has not picked one.

Open **Configure** on the SunBridge entry, choose **Advanced**, and enter the serial of each datalogger you own (it is on the datalogger's label and on its device page). This message goes away once the list is set. Delete the device of any datalogger that is not yours.

port_rollback_failed.title: {title} is not listening
port_rollback_failed.description:
Changing the port to {new_port} failed, and going back to port {port} failed too, so SunBridge is not listening and no datalogger data arrives.

Free port {port} (stop whatever else is using it), then reload SunBridge from its integration page, or use **Reconfigure** to choose another free port and set the same **Server port** on the datalogger. This message clears itself as soon as SunBridge listens again.

datalogger_silent.title: {name} has stopped sending data
datalogger_silent.description:
SunBridge has received nothing from {name} for {hours} hours of daylight, when the inverter should be producing.

Check that the datalogger has power and a network connection, that its **Server IP** still points at this Home Assistant and its **Server port** is {port}, and that nothing on your network blocks that port.

This message clears itself as soon as the datalogger connects again. If the datalogger was replaced or removed, delete its device on the SunBridge integration page instead.
